epic.title: FixForward: one item from record to live listing, then the pilot
epic.description:
FixForward sells Phil's and the household's own things on his eBay UK private account now (RAM, graphics cards, shoes, clothing, anything else), and later buys faulty items to repair and resell: "1 and 2 into 3", on 2 to 5 hours a week. Every listing is drafted and he approves it; he sets every price, with sold data as guidance; offers at or above his floor auto-accept; common questions get templates; labels are bought on his confirm; buying is alert only. It runs on the PC worker with the cloud receiving eBay's notifications, keeps its data in Mycelium's database under its own prefix, and shows on a Mycelium page with Telegram approvals. Until the first slice (one item from record to live listing) ships, FixForward is the only venture (H6). The repo at A:\Projects\fixforward and its roadmap (phases 0 to 6, to 2027-02-26) are the plan; these tickets mirror it and add what the brief decided.

## Order
First the decisions and Phil's queue: fixf.01 (trading rules and the contract), fixf.02 (the medical display), fixf.03 (official API only), fixf.04 (developer keyset), fixf.05 (business policies), fixf.06 (basket), fixf.07 (Saturday rehearsal), fixf.08 (the three certain risks), fixf.09 and fixf.10 (brand and voice). Then fixf.11 (token and policies, after mail.22), fixf.12 (the live test, the fork), fixf.13 (outcome B if needed) and fixf.34 (the first slice done). In parallel the Mycelium build: fixf.14 (tables), fixf.15 (import), fixf.16 (page), fixf.17 (Telegram), then fixf.18 to fixf.27. Then fixf.28 (pilot and dry run) and fixf.33 (scale-up and the 2027-02-26 decision). fixf.29, fixf.30, fixf.31 and fixf.32 fit in anywhere.

## Done means
One item went from inventory record to live listing by the rules (fixf.34); the pilot passed its dry-run week (fixf.28); and on 2027-02-26 Phil has the total raised, hours, pounds per hour and sell-through, and has decided private or business (fixf.33).

## Flags
- Section 3 item 20 [claude]: tables inside Mycelium mean the migrations and RLS invariants apply, one migrations owner, deny-all plus service_role, own prefix (fixf.14). Not reopened.
- Section 3 item 26 [claude]: "plus scraping" is declined by the repo's rule; fixf.03 records the cautious version and Phil can overturn it.
- H10 flag 1 [claude]: the employment contract's side-work terms are checked in fixf.01 before any buying automation.
- H10 flag 2 [claude]: the medical display stays out of inventory until its ownership is confirmed in writing (fixf.02).
- Hard rules on every eBay ticket: official API only, never scrape; nothing on the live account without Phil's yes; no buyer data stored; never below floor; no Vinted automation; secrets only in Credential Manager.

## Dossier
The dossier is attached in Docs: (link filled by the integrator).

tickets.title: Research: trading rules (eBay business expectation, HMRC trading allowance, the 30-sales report) and the employment contract's side-work terms, before any buying automation
tickets.description:
## What
Write one page, in Mycelium's docs and attached to this ticket, answering four questions for FixForward as it stands and as Phil plans it. (1) When eBay UK expects a business account: its business seller policy names selling items bought to resell, making items to sell and buying for a business; say which of Phil's planned activities (selling household belongings, repairing his own items, buying faulty items to repair and resell, buy alerts) cross that line. (2) HMRC: personal possessions usually carry no Income Tax; the trading allowance is £1,000 a year now and the GOV.UK policy paper of 28 October 2026 raises it to £3,000 from 6 April 2027; capital gains on any single item over £6,000. (3) eBay's digital sales report to HMRC: 30 sales or £1,707 after fees in a calendar year, the NI number and bank account reported, payout holds if the details are not given. (4) The employment contract: a checklist of the clauses Phil reads himself (exclusivity, outside work, conflict of interest, use of employer equipment, the handbook if the contract refers to one), with a yes or no line for each that he fills in. Claude never reads the contract unless Phil hands it over.

## Why
Phil's answer 3.23 asked for a research ticket first, before any buying automation; the H10 flag put the contract check into it because the goal is "growing into a business".

## Done looks like
The page exists with sources dated; each of the four questions has a plain answer and the date checked; the contract checklist has Phil's yes or no on every line; the ticket comment says whether buy alerts (fixf.23) and repairs of bought items (fixf.24) may proceed on a private account.

## Unlocks
fixf.23 (buy alerts may be built); fixf.24 (repairs of bought items); fin.26 (tax on side income, shared: the same page answers both).

## Depends on
Nothing. The research is done from GOV.UK, eBay help pages and Phil's own contract.

## Flag
H10 flag 1 [claude], not reopened: the side-work terms in the employment contract are checked here, before any buying automation.

Hard rules from the FixForward repo (CLAUDE.md and selling-rules.md v1.5), binding on this ticket: eBay only through its official API, never drive, script, scrape or fetch the eBay site, its search, sold prices, seller pages or Seller Hub; nothing changes on the live eBay account without Phil's yes to that specific action (publish, revise, end, offer, message, feedback, order, cancellation, refund); no eBay user data (buyer names, usernames, addresses, order or message contents) stored on disk or in any database; never price, offer or accept below an item's floor; no automation operates Vinted; secrets live only in Windows Credential Manager through the repo's scripts and are never printed, logged, committed or pasted.

Phil's answer 3.26 was "official eBay APIs, plus scraping where they fall short".
